flashcard_questions.q: A type of extended metaphor where an object or idea represents something beyond its literal meaning. Throughout Macbeth, darkness symbolises evil, guilt, and the concealment of sin.
When the audience knows something that a character on stage does not. Here, the audience knows Macbeth is planning Duncan’s murder while Banquo does not.
A speech delivered by a character alone on stage, revealing their inner thoughts directly to the audience. Macbeth’s dagger soliloquy reveals his psychological torment before the murder.

flashcard_questions.a: References within a text to other well-known stories, myths, or figures. Macbeth alludes to Hecate (goddess of witchcraft), wolves and Tarquin to align himself with evil forces.
A pair of rhyming lines that appear together, often used to create a sense of finality. Macbeth’s couplet about the bell seals Duncan’s fate.
